2000-12-26: Phil Spector, described as celebrating his 60th birthday on Boxing Day, continued to make late-night phone calls outlining plans to revive past musical splendours.
2001-11-15: An appeal court in Manhattan ordered Phil Spector to pay $3 million to the Ronettes for unpaid royalties from commercial use of their recordings, upholding a lower court ruling that he broke his 1963 contract with the group.
2003-02-03: Record producer Phil Spector was charged with murder in connection with the death of a woman found shot at his home in a Los Angeles suburb.
Actress Lana Clarkson was found shot dead at Phil Spector's Hollywood mansion, and Spector was subsequently arrested for her murder.
2003-02-04: Record producer Phil Spector was arrested in connection with the shooting death of actress Lana Clarkson at his Los Angeles mansion and released on $1m bail.
2003-02-06: Phil Spector, who produced Starsailor's forthcoming second album, has been arrested.
2003-02-13: Phil Spector's friend says his defense will claim the fatal shooting of actress Lana Clarkson at his home was an accident.
2003-09-22: The Los Angeles coroner's office ruled the death of actress Lana Clarkson at Phil Spector's home a homicide, contradicting Spector's claim that she committed suicide.
2003-11-05: Bobby Hatfield, the singer known for his falsetto on the Righteous Brothers' Phil Spector-produced hit "You've Lost That Lovin' Feeling," died aged 63.
2003-11-14: The Beatles' album Let It Be... Naked is released, presenting a version of Let It Be closer to the band's original intentions and removing Phil Spector's production.
2003-11-20: Phil Spector was charged with the murder of actress Lana Clarkson, who died at his home in February.
2003-11-21: Phil Spector told his chauffeur he thought he had "killed somebody" the night an actress was shot at his Californian mansion, according to a police report.
2004-05-07: Phil Spector's defence lawyers say medical experts they consulted concluded that actor Lana Clarkson may have shot herself, contradicting the coroner's murder finding in the case for which Spector was charged.
2004-09-27: Phil Spector pleaded not guilty to murder after being indicted in connection with the death of actor Lana Clarkson.
2005-01-07: Newly released grand jury transcripts show Phil Spector initially told police he accidentally shot Lana Clarkson, though he has since suggested she committed suicide.
2005-03-08: Phil Spector restated that he had nothing to do with the death of Lana Clarkson and is awaiting trial for her murder.
2005-10-13: Phil Spector's defence attorneys argue in court papers that his incriminating statements should be thrown out because he was suffering withdrawal symptoms from prescription drugs when he told police he had shot and killed a woman in 2003.
2005-10-25: Lawyers for Phil Spector request that his apparent admission of guilt to police at the scene be ruled inadmissible in his upcoming murder trial.
2007-03-19: Jury selection began in the murder trial of music producer Phil Spector, four years after actor Lana Clarkson was shot to death in the foyer of his home.
2007-04-02: Jury selection for Phil Spector's murder trial is expected to begin, and a new biography of Spector is scheduled for publication.
2007-04-19: A jury of nine men and three women was sworn in for the murder trial of music producer Phil Spector, with proceedings ordered to commence the following Monday.
2007-04-25: Phil Spector's murder trial opened in Los Angeles, where prosecutors described him as "sinister and deadly" for the 2003 shooting death of Lana Clarkson, to which he pleaded not guilty.
2007-04-26: In Phil Spector's murder trial, a former girlfriend testified that he threatened her with a revolver and a shotgun during a 1993 encounter.
2007-04-28: Phil Spector is on trial in a California courtroom for the alleged murder of a woman, with jury selection and opening statements underway.
2007-05-05: Phil Spector is standing trial for the murder of Lana Clarkson, following his arrest a few months after a 25-year-silence-breaking interview with journalist Mick Brown.
2007-05-07: In Phil Spector's murder trial, a second witness, Diane Ogden, testified that Spector once held a gun to her head and threatened to kill her at his home in 1989.
2007-05-09: Two more women testified at Phil Spector's murder trial that he threatened them with guns, bringing to four the number of prosecution witnesses describing a pattern of gun threats before the 2003 death of Lana Clarkson.
2007-05-10: A friend testified at Phil Spector's murder trial that he was "not his usual self" during a dinner hours before Lana Clarkson was shot dead at his mansion.
2007-05-29: A coroner testified in Phil Spector's murder trial that Lana Clarkson's injuries were consistent with homicide, contradicting the defense's suicide claim.
2007-06-14: In Phil Spector's murder trial, a coroner's criminalist denied compromising evidence while collecting fibres from Lana Clarkson's dress, as defense lawyers argued crucial forensic evidence was compromised.
2007-06-26: Phil Spector granted the BBC his first extensive interview in 35 years for a BBC2 Arena documentary, conducted at his Los Angeles home while he was on trial for murder.

Lawyers for Phil Spector claimed in the opening day of the defence's argument at his Los Angeles murder trial that Lana Clarkson committed suicide, presenting a forensics expert who said the scientific evidence indicated suicide.
2007-07-11: Witnesses at Phil Spector's murder trial testified about the depressed state of Lana Clarkson, the actor found dead at his mansion, as the defense contends she killed herself.
2007-09-18: The jury in Phil Spector's murder trial declared it was unable to reach a verdict after seven days of deliberation, with the judge considering allowing the lesser charge of involuntary manslaughter.
2007-09-20: The judge in the Phil Spector murder trial issued new jury instructions after the panel reported it was deadlocked 7-5, and deliberations resumed.
2007-09-26: Phil Spector's murder trial ended in a mistrial after the jury declared itself deadlocked.
2007-09-27: Phil Spector's murder trial is declared a mistrial, with the Los Angeles district attorney seeking a retrial.
2008-02-17: Phil Spector is about to break his media silence with a BBC2 television interview about the murder case against him and his career, ahead of his retrial later in the year.
2008-03-19: Judge Larry Paul Fidler rejected a defence motion accusing him of bias in Phil Spector's murder case, denying the request for a new judge ahead of the retrial.
2008-05-08: Larry Levine, Phil Spector's studio engineer during the Wall of Sound era, died at his home in Encino, California, on his 80th birthday.
2008-10-24: Phil Spector gives his first lengthy television interview for a BBC2 documentary, in which he protests his innocence in the death of Lana Clarkson and compares his work to Leonardo da Vinci.
2009-02-11: Ronettes singer Estelle Bennett, who sang backing vocals on Phil Spector's 1963 hit Be My Baby, was found dead at her New Jersey home at age 67.
2009-04-13: Music producer Phil Spector was convicted of second-degree murder for shooting actor Lana Clarkson at his mansion six years earlier.
2009-04-14: Music producer Phil Spector was convicted of murder.
2009-05-29: Phil Spector was sentenced to life in prison with a minimum of 19 years for the murder of actress Lana Clarkson.
2009-06-08: Phil Spector begins his 19-year sentence for the murder of Lana Clarkson, as his wife Rachelle Spector condemns prison conditions and maintains his innocence.
2009-08-20: Phil Spector expressed fears for his safety while serving a prison sentence for the murder of actress Lana Clarkson and said he wanted to move to a different jail.
2010-03-23: Phil Spector was reportedly beaten up by a fellow inmate in prison, though his wife denied he was assaulted and prison officials said they had no reports of any altercations involving him.
2010-10-12: Al Pacino will reportedly play Phil Spector in an HBO Films biopic about Spector's life, with Barry Levinson directing and David Mamet writing, though the film is in development and no release date has been given.
2012-02-04: The mother of Lana Clarkson, the actress murdered by Phil Spector, settled her wrongful death civil case against Spector, with the terms not disclosed.
2012-02-21: The US Supreme Court declined to hear Phil Spector's appeal against his 2009 murder conviction.
2014-03-10: Ronnie Spector's audiovisual show Beyond the Beehive recounts her life and marriage to Phil Spector, including his withholding of permission for her to perform the Ronettes' signature hits.
